title: The local term at a point component
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $s$-scheme. Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible cohomological correspondence, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ be its coefficient morphism, and let $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$. Suppose that $\beta\subseteq F$ is an open-and-closed subscheme with $\beta\simeq\Spec k$ over $s$, finite étale over $s$ of relative dimension $0$ (for instance a component $\beta\in\pi_0(F)$ of this form when $F$ is proper with finitely many open-and-closed components, or the reduced point component $B_{\bar x}$ of a point $\bar x$ of $F$). Then the local term $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\int_\beta(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta)$ of [def-trf-local-term], where $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$, is the element of $A$ corresponding to the trace class $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta$ under the canonical identification

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\beta,A)}\bigl(A_\beta,\omega_{\beta,A}\bigr)
\cong\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A
$$

of the point case $\beta\simeq\Spec k$. In particular this computes $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u)=\operatorname{LT}_{B_{\bar x}}(u)$ at every point $\bar x$ with reduced open-and-closed point component $B_{\bar x}$.

proof.text: The data of [def-trf-correspondence] include the separated finite-type support $C$, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$. By [prop-trf-trace-class-unconditional] the class of [def-trf-trace-class] is a morphism $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$. Its restriction to the clopen $\beta$ is the morphism $\tau=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_\beta\to\omega_{\beta,A}$ defined in [def-trf-local-term]. The structure morphism $a=a_\beta:\beta\to s$ is an isomorphism, by the given isomorphism over $s$. In particular it is proper: in the definitions collected by [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] an isomorphism has closed diagonal, is finite type (the identity algebra is finitely generated), and remains a closed map after every base change. It is also finite etale of relative dimension zero, as in the hypothesis. The admissibility datum for this separated finite-type structure morphism is available by [def-trf-admissibility]; it is the constructible adjunction, not an unrestricted ambient adjoint. Thus the local-term and integration definitions apply, with their specified exceptional adjunction.

source.place: first sentences: existence of the trace class and the point component

proof.text: By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], $\omega_{\beta,A}=Ra^!A_s$. The relative-dimension-zero purity clause of [prop-functor-package] gives the normalized identification $\omega_{\beta,A}\cong A_\beta$, with no twist or shift. Apply [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] to the isomorphism $a$: its exact mutually inverse functors on module sheaves, preserving the constant coefficient sheaves, act degreewise on complexes and preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Their inverse identifications therefore descend to derived categories and identify $\operatorname{End}(A_\beta)$ with $\operatorname{End}(A_s)$. The finite-coefficient equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], whose functor is evaluation at $s$ as specified in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], sends $A_s$ to the complex $A[0]$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\beta,A)}(A_\beta,\omega_{\beta,A})\cong\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A)\cong A$: First [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], applied to the abelian category of $A$-modules, identifies $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A[0])$ with $\operatorname{End}_A(A)$. The final map evaluates an $A$-linear endomorphism at $1$, and its inverse sends $b$ to multiplication by $b$: $f(r)=rf(1)$ for every $r\in A$. The identifications are $A$-linear, since inverse image and evaluation act termwise on module maps and therefore send $bf$ to $b$ times the image of $f$, and the single-complex functor does the same. These objects are constructible, so their Hom groups agree with those in the full ambient derived categories.

source.place: dimension-zero purity and the displayed Hom identification

proof.text: Let $e:A_\beta\to\omega_{\beta,A}$ correspond to $1$ under Step 2, that is, the purity map $\gamma_{a,A_s}$. By [def-trf-integration], $\int_\beta e$ is the ordinary pullback unit, followed by $R\Gamma(e)$ and the exceptional counit. The last two arrows are $R\Gamma(s,-)$ of the smooth trace $\varepsilon_a\circ Ra_!(\gamma_{a,A_s})$ of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. For finite etale $a$, [det-sp-trace-basic], clauses (1) and (3), identifies exactly this purity-transported counit with summation over the fibres. Here $a$ has one sheet, so the ordinary pullback unit sends $r$ to its single copy $r$, and summation sends that copy to $r$. Thus $\int_\beta e=1$. This uses the normalized finite-etale trace, rather than identifying the ordinary unit with an exceptional unit. Every morphism corresponding to $b\in A$ in Step 2 is $be$; [lem-trf-integration-linear] gives $\int_\beta(be)=b$. No field assumption on $A$ or division by a degree is used.

source.place: integration of the unit section and linearity (correcting the adjunction explanation)

proof.text: Take the section $\tau=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ from Step 1 in the scalar calculation of Step 3. The equality $\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u)=\int_\beta\tau$ in [def-trf-local-term] gives precisely the claimed scalar under Step 2. For a reduced clopen point component $B_{\bar x}$, the same definition gives $B_{\bar x}\simeq\Spec k$ and $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u)=\operatorname{LT}_{B_{\bar x}}(u)$, so this instance proves the final assertion.

source.place: final specialization to the local term

No new nodes. proof_deps equals the union of step uses. All cited ids exist and none is merged. A transitive walk over all cited deps never reaches the item, so there is no cycle. Statement: only the binders X, C, K, u and A=A_{E,n} were made explicit, and they match def-trf-correspondence. 'beta ≃ Spec k over s' is automatic because k is algebraically closed. No hypothesis was added, none dropped, the conclusion is not weakened, and F need not be proper. Step 1: the trace class is defined (prop-trf-trace-class-unconditional, def-trf-trace-class) and restricted as in def-trf-local-term. The isomorphism a is proper and admissible, as def-trf-local-term requires. Step 2: omega = Ra^!A_s ≅ A_beta by prop-functor-package(6) in dimension 0. The Hom group is identified with A through the isomorphism inverse-image equivalence (2),(3), Fib_s = Gamma(s,-) (lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point), and the Mathlib leaf for single-functor full faithfulness (FullyFaithful.lean:37/45, checked). A-linearity is argued. Step 3: the integral of e = gamma is eps∘Ra_!(gamma)∘P_a∘eta. Its last two arrows are Tr^sm_a of def-pur-smooth-trace (smooth separated, d=0, same constructible counit). det-sp-trace-basic(3) identifies Tr^sm_a with summation over the fibres. Summation after the unit multiplies by the degree, which is 1. lem-trf-integration-linear then gives the integral of b·e = b. No division is used. Step 4 is an elementary substitution, and the B_x clause comes from def-trf-local-term. Confirmed source error: the blueprint calls the La^*⊣Ra_* unit the unit of Ra_!⊣Ra^! and uses a triangle identity, which is a type mismatch. The delivery repairs this via the normalized finite-etale trace, with the statement unchanged; the unit has no steps, so no route is replaced.
